item.title: Marcos Jnr promised a ‘new Philippines’. What happened?
item.description: “I knew your parents very well and they were great,” US President Donald Trump told his Philippine counterpart at a dinner in Manila this week, offering a glowing tribute to a family that was once forced into exile in disgrace. Turning to his host, Ferdinand “Bongbong” Marcos Jnr, Trump recalled his friendship with the Philippine leader’s parents, the late dictator Ferdinand Marcos Snr and his wife Imelda. “It’s a true pleasure to be back in the Philippines. item.title: Russian missiles land in Poland, as Europe holds military drills nearby
item.description: Two Russian missiles and a suspected drone came down in Poland on Friday in what its prime minister said was likely to be a provocation timed to coincide with European military exercises in his country for a possible post-war mission in Ukraine. The incidents occurred while Russia carried out a major nighttime bombardment of neighbouring Ukraine. item.title: Hong Kong looks to community networks to support Tai Po fire survivors’ mental health
item.description: More than 3,000 survivors of Hong Kong’s deadly Wang Fuk Court fire have received mental health support from authorities in the past year, with some experiencing fewer symptoms of post-traumatic stress disorder (PTSD) after psychological intervention. Dr Lam Ching-choi, chairman of the Advisory Committee on Mental Health, said on Friday that the government would study whether existing community networks could continue to offer mental health support to people affected by the fire. item.title: Princeton PhD student from China detained by ICE after US academic conference
item.description: A Chinese PhD student at Princeton University, New Jersey, was detained by US Immigration and Customs Enforcement (ICE) on Thursday after presenting her research at a neuroscience conference in Washington, the South China Morning Post has confirmed. item.title: Can China’s top-down military adapt to the speed of AI and drone warfare?
item.description: Drawing on lessons from the Ukraine war, Chinese military commentators are calling for frontline commanders to have greater freedom to make battlefield decisions without waiting for orders from above, as drones and AI accelerate the pace of combat.
